bib.title: Train Short, Test Long: Attention with Linear Biases Enables Input Length Extrapolation

question: Can a transformer LM trained on short sequences be applied to longer ones at inference, and which position method enables this efficiently?
hypothesis: Extrapolation depends on the position method; a non-learned linear distance penalty on attention scores (recency bias) will extrapolate without runtime cost.
contributions: Show sinusoidal, rotary and T5 bias extrapolate poorly or slowly
Introduce ALiBi, a static linear attention bias with no position embeddings
Show ALiBi extrapolates and trains faster/leaner on WikiText-103, Toronto BookCorpus and a 1.3B model on CC100+RoBERTa
Analysis that gains from longer Lvalid largely reflect reduced early token curse

method.summary: Replace position embeddings in the Baevski & Auli LM with ALiBi: add m*[-(i-1),...,0] to query-key scores per head with fixed geometric slopes. Train at L in 64..3072 on WikiText-103, then evaluate at longer Lvalid; repeat on Toronto BookCorpus and a 1.3B model on CC100+RoBERTa.
method.task: next-token language modelling, perplexity vs input length

datasets.name: Toronto BookCorpus
datasets.split: same split as Khandelwal et al. (2020)
datasets.preprocessing: BERT vocabulary of 29K byte-pair encodings (Khandelwal et al. tokenization)

datasets.name: CC100+RoBERTa
datasets.source: RoBERTa corpus (161 GB: Toronto Book Corpus, English Wikipedia, CC-News, OpenWebText, Stories) plus English CC-100 (300 GB)

models.name: Baevski & Auli transformer LM with ALiBi / sinusoidal / rotary / T5 bias
models.architecture: decoder-only transformer, tied embedding and softmax
models.context: trained L=64 to 3072; evaluated up to 16k

other.slopes: geometric sequence 2^(-8/n) start and ratio for n heads; 8 heads: 1/2^1 .. 1/2^8
16 heads: 8 slopes interpolated by geometric averaging, start 1/2^0.5, ratio 1/sqrt2

training.hardware: WikiText-103: one V100 GPU (32GB per Fig 1); 1.3B: 128 V100 GPUs
training.compute: 1.3B: roughly 5.5k to 6.7k hours per run (Tables 11-12 'Hours' column, unit not printed)
training.seeds: other than position method and training length, no other hyperparameters changed, including the random seed; sinusoidal L=3072 std dev 0.24

other.note: optimizer, lr, batch size, dropout inherited from Baevski & Auli (2018) and not restated

inference.decoding: perplexity scoring; nonoverlapping inference by default; sliding window with stride S=1 or 512 in the analysis

metrics.name: perplexity
metrics.definition: exp of mean next-token loss on the validation or test set, at a chosen Lvalid

metrics.name: training/inference speed
metrics.definition: words per second on one V100

eval.protocol: Single run per configuration, except sinusoidal L=3072 std dev (0.24) reported. Sinusoidal baselines on CC100+RoBERTa are stopped at equal training time in Table 11.

results.claim: 1.3B ALiBi (L=1024) reaches slightly lower validation perplexity than sinusoidal (L=2048) at Lvalid=2048 with 3.1 GB less memory.
results.setup: CC100+RoBERTa, 1.3B, 50k updates (1 epoch), equal training time
results.quote: outperforms by 0.09 perplexity the sinusoidal model trained on L = 2048

results.claim: Abstract: 1.3B model trained on 1024 extrapolates to 2048, matching sinusoidal L=2048 perplexity with 11% faster training and 11% less memory.
results.setup: 1.3B model, CC100+RoBERTa 461 GB, 50k updates, 128 V100, Lvalid=2048
results.quote:
training 11% faster and
using 11% less memory
results.note: Table 11 memory is 26.2 GB vs 29.3 GB (about 10.6%); Fig 5 caption says 6%-11% less memory.

results.claim: ALiBi L=1024 model reaches a given perplexity on average 11% faster than sinusoidal L=2048.
results.setup: CC100+RoBERTa, 1.3B, five evenly spaced points through training
results.quote: reaches a given perplexity value, on average, 11% faster than the sinusoidal model does

results.claim: Sinusoidal model trained on 512 cannot extrapolate: it improves only until k=20, is steady to k=50, then degrades.
results.quote: performance stops improving and stays steady from k = 20 to k = 50 and then begins degrading

results.claim: On WikiText-103, ALiBi trained at L=512 gets 18.40 validation perplexity at Lvalid=3072, better than the sinusoidal L=3072 model.
results.quote: achieves a perplexity score of 18.40 on the development set when extrapolating to subsequences of length 3072

results.claim: ALiBi L=3072 gets 17.60 vs sinusoidal 18.67 at Lvalid=3072 without extrapolation.
ALiBi L=512 model is 1.84 times faster to train than L=3072 sinusoidal and still beats it at Lvalid=3072.
results.quote: The L = 512 model is 1.84 times faster to train

results.claim: ALiBi adds no runtime or parameters and 0-0.7% memory over sinusoidal at the same L.
T5 bias training is at least twice as slow as sinusoidal: 14.4k WPS (L=512) vs 28.5k WPS (sinusoidal L=1024).
results.quote: L = 512 T5 bias model runs at 14.4k WPS

results.claim: Test perplexity on WikiText-103: ALiBi L=3072 18.30 vs sinusoidal 19.38, rotary 19.28, T5 bias 18.73.
results.table: Table 6, rows Sinusoidal, Rotary, T5 Bias, ALiBi L = 3072, column Test (19.38, 19.28, 18.73, 18.30)

results.claim: With sliding-window evaluation (S=1), ALiBi perplexity stays flat as Lvalid grows (L=512: 17.98 at 512 to 18.3 at 3072) while sinusoidal explodes (18.35 to 360.12), so the gain from longer Lvalid under nonoverlapping evaluation is attributed to the early token curse.

limits: Authors' analysis (App B): gains from Lvalid > L under nonoverlapping evaluation largely come from reduced early token curse; with sliding window S=1 ALiBi stays flat, so it may not use contexts longer than trained.
On the 1.3B model ALiBi performs similarly to sinusoidal at equal L, not better; advantage on small data is conjectured to be an inductive bias benefit.
Optimizer and learning-rate settings are not stated (inherited from Baevski & Auli).
Rotary was run with unoptimised code, about 2% slower after optimisation per footnote 5.
Slopes were set by manual exploration of about ten sets on WikiText-103; one run on Books used them untuned.

terms.definition: a model's ability to continue performing well as the number of input tokens during validation increases beyond the number of tokens on which the model was trained
predictions early in each subsequence cannot access many previous context tokens, increasing perplexity
